resources.text: Two examples with te: Example A appears in a registry-address box: te Mira (membership unverified). Example B appears in a casual play dialogue: te friend, come sit here. Both are acceptable as written.

nal-sources/convention.text: Fictional Nal convention, complete excerpt: In registry-address boxes, te marks a verified member; use se when membership is unverified. In casual dialogue, te is also a familiar greeting and does not assert membership. These are context-specific uses; the registry rule does not prohibit the casual greeting.

nal-sources/contexts.text: Original teaching panel A is labelled registry-address box and explicitly says membership unverified. Panel B is labelled casual play dialogue; no registry entry or membership assertion accompanies it. The public post omitted neither label, but grouped both examples as acceptable.
